86	## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
    87	- Purpose: measure, before any prediction or method exists, how much more throughput one GPU gives when the unchanged published command runs several times at once. This measured factor is the only source of same-GPU headroom for bounds. No model call is involved.
    88	- When the profile command exits 0 and the profile gate passes, the pipeline uploads trusted `m5/concurrency_probe.py` to remote `profiler/` and, through boxrun as operation `concurrency` with the resolved `profile` budget, runs `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py harness/run_command.sh out/concurrency <budget_s>` from the shared run directory. Remote `out/concurrency/` is cleared first. Fetched files land in `A/results/profile/out/concurrency/`; the log is `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. There is no agent repair and no execution retry. Probe receipts count toward profile v1 `usd` and `gpu_s` like other box receipts.
    89	- Each invocation runs `bash harness/run_command.sh` with its working directory set to a fresh `concurrency-work/<label>/` under the shared run directory. That directory holds a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work` and `evaluation-work`, plus an empty `out/` directory. Labels are `single-1`, `single-2`, `single-3`, `n2-1`, `n2-2`, `n4-1` to `n4-4`. Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<label>.log` of the shared run directory. The environment is inherited unchanged apart from the MPS variables below. Nsight is not used.
    90	- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
    91	- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
    92	- Sequence: three single runs one after another, then 2 copies started together, then 4 copies started together. Wall seconds come from a monotonic clock around each subprocess; a batch's wall runs from launching its first copy to the exit of its last. `T1` is the median of the single walls. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. A batch counts only when every copy exits 0. For a counted batch, `factor_n = n * T1 / wall_n`.
    93	- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
    94	  - `mps`: boolean, true when the recorded measurements ran under MPS; `mps_failed`: boolean;
    95	  - `single_wall_s`: array of exactly three entries, each a finite positive number or null (failed or not run);
    96	  - `batches`: exactly two rows, in order n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`; `wall_s` and `factor` are finite positive numbers or null, `all_ok` and `skipped` are booleans, and `factor` is null unless the batch counted;
    97	  - `factor`: the largest counted `factor_n`, or null when any single run failed or no batch counted.
    98	  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
    99	- The probe never fails the profile stage and never changes the profile gate. A probe timeout, nonzero exit, or missing or invalid file gives packet `concurrency: null` and `headroom: null`. The pipeline validates the file against the exact shape above before copying it into the packet.

     2	# run_evaluation.sh - published-baseline evaluation adapter (PINDER FroDock baseline).
     3	#
     4	# Invoked from a fresh evaluation working directory that links baseline-published/, method/, data/,
     5	# harness/ and payload/, with absolute BASELINE_DIR, METHOD_DIR, BASELINE_OUT, METHOD_OUT, EVAL_OUT and
     6	#   EVAL_MODE            equivalence | warmup | performance | curve
     7	#   EVAL_PROTOCOL        path to the sealed protocol JSON (timing_scope is copied from it verbatim)
     8	#   EVAL_INPUTS          JSON: {"ids": [input_id, ...], ...}; an input_id is a PINDER system ID, optionally
     9	#                        suffixed ":holo" / ":apo" (or "/holo", "/apo") to restrict the pairing
    10	#   EVAL_SEEDS           JSON: {"kind":"paired_median","seeds":[...]} or {"kind":"deterministic",...}
    11	#   EVAL_COMPUTE_BUDGET  GPU-second budget (curve mode only)
    12	#
    13	# For every seed (outer loop) and input id (inner loop) it runs the published configuration unchanged:
    14	# `pinder_methods preprocess` (holo and apo, untimed setup), `pinder_methods predict --method frodock`
    15	# with n_solutions=50, mpi_np=8, force=false (timed), and `pinder_eval` on that run's own decoys.
    16	# FroDock exposes no seed; the seed is recorded and exported as BASELINE_EVAL_SEED only.
    17	# Writes $EVAL_OUT/evaluation.json:
    18	#   {records:[{input_id,seed,metrics:{...}}], timing_scope, gpu_count, wall_s, compute_budget}
    19	# wall_s = sum of the timed predict invocations (process launch, MPI startup, all 8 FroDock stages,
    20	# decoy writing and copy-out included). The baseline uses no GPU (gpu_count 0, 0 GPU-seconds), so a
    21	# curve budget in GPU seconds is never consumed; it is checked and recorded.
    22	# CUDA MPS variables are inherited unchanged.

    25	: "${EVAL_OUT:?EVAL_OUT must be set}"
    26	: "${EVAL_PROTOCOL:?EVAL_PROTOCOL must be set}"

    31	case "$EVAL_MODE" in equivalence|warmup|performance|curve) ;; *) echo "ERROR: unknown EVAL_MODE $EVAL_MODE" >&2; exit 2;; esac
    32	if [ "$EVAL_MODE" = curve ] && [ -z "$EVAL_COMPUTE_BUDGET" ]; then echo "ERROR: curve mode needs EVAL_COMPUTE_BUDGET" >&2; exit 2; fi

1	Can increased parallelism in protein–protein docking improve the recovery of experimentally observed binding poses, particularly for AAV capsid–receptor interactions? We want to investigate whether additional parallel computation improves scientific results, rather than simply accelerating an existing search.
     2	
     3	Use PINDER-S as the primary benchmark: https://github.com/pinder-org/pinder
     4	
     5	It contains 250 protein–protein test complexes, including 93 with paired unbound structures. Prioritise those 93 cases for realistic docking evaluation. Use the published AAV–AAVR structures 6IHB, 6JCQ and 6JCS as a separate, biologically motivated challenge.
     6	
     7	These represent AAV2–PKD2, AAV1–PKD2 and AAV5–PKD1 interactions. The AAV challenge should initially evaluate redocking from separated components. Do not treat these as independently determined unbound structures.
     8	
     9	Investigate the following questions:
    10	- Can existing docking methods recover known protein–protein interfaces from the benchmark inputs?
    11	- What limits the number of independent candidate poses that can be evaluated or searched concurrently?
    12	- Could restructuring the search exploit massively parallel GPU hardware rather than merely distributing independent runs?
    13	- Does additional search improve the probability of recovering experimentally observed interfaces within a fixed time or compute budget?
    14	
    15	Evaluate scientific correctness using DockQ, interface RMSD and native-contact recovery. DockQ ≥ 0.23 defines an acceptable-quality prediction under the standard benchmark convention. Compare the top-ranked predicted pose and the best pose among a fixed number of generated candidates. Do not conflate search coverage with ranking quality.
    16	
    17	Compare wall-clock time, cost, search throughput and time to an acceptable pose against an optimised existing implementation.
    18	
    19	Use independent random seeds and a fixed, preregistered selection of benchmark cases.
    20	
    21	Begin with small calibration experiments to establish scientific validity, input sizes and actual performance.
    22	
    23	Use those measurements to formulate a larger experimental proposal within a $1,000 compute budget.
    24	
    25	Do not infer BBB transcytosis, binding affinity or therapeutic relevance from docking accuracy alone.
    26	
    27	Explicitly report when the benchmarks or available structures cannot support a scientific conclusion.

3:## Run identity and agent chat names
4:- `args.blind` is a boolean, default false. `args.raid`, when supplied, is a non-empty single-line string and takes precedence over automatic selection. `launch.js stage --stage m5` also accepts `--raid <name>` and `--blind`.
5:- `m5/raids.json` is `{theme, public, blind}`: a theme string and two ordered arrays of base names. The heist theme uses separate public and blind lists. Automatic selection skips names already present in `m5/raids_used.jsonl`; after the base names it cycles through the same list with suffixes `2`, `3`, etc. Explicit names are recorded too.
6:- Each ledger row and `C/raid.json` has exactly `{raid, blind, run_root, utc}`; `run_root` is absolute and `utc` is an ISO UTC timestamp. Reservations are serialised. A run reuses its existing reservation and rejects conflicting raid/blind arguments. The launcher reserves against the original pipeline ledger before freezing its copy.
7:- m5 sets `args.chat_prefix = "x-<raid>"`. Other scripts opt in using `args.chat_prefix`, an agent option `chat_prefix`, or the workflow flag `--chat-prefix`. Without a prefix, runner naming stays unchanged.
8:- Names are `<chat_prefix>-<label>[-<descriptor>]`; labels are lowercased, non-`[a-z0-9-]` runs become `-`, edge hyphens are removed, and an empty label becomes `agent`. Concurrent sibling calls sharing a label within a stage add `1of<n>`, `2of<n>`, etc. Repair turns add `retry<k>` (starting at 1); fallback calls add `fb`. When needed together, descriptors appear in that order, separated by hyphens. Harness repair calls supply agent option `retry: 1`.
9:- wf passes the name to every runner as `name`. OpenCode uses `--title`, Claude uses `--name`, and Codex prepends `[<name>]` as the first prompt line, before role instructions.
11:## m5 model policy (workflow configuration)
12:- m5 runs use `node idea/wf.js --config m5/wf_config.json --script m5/pipeline.js ... --profile latent_skeptic --family codex`, without `--disable-family claude`. `m5/wf_config.json` holds a `workflow` section identical to `idea/config.json`'s and an `understudy` section with: `primary_family: "codex"`, `mode: "fallback"`, `on_refusal: "halt"`, `disabled_families: []`, `chain: {"codex": ["opencode"], "opencode": ["codex"], "claude": ["codex"], "cursor": ["codex"]}`, and `routes: [{"match": "^skeptic-[45]$", "primary": "claude/sonnet"}, {"match": "^review$", "primary": "claude/sonnet"}, {"match": "^(intake|harness|[a-z]+-repair|seal|propose|tests|implement)$", "understudy": "claude/opus"}]`.
13:- Effect: every authoring call (intake, harness, any `*-repair`, seal, propose, tests, implement) resolves to a Codex primary with `claude/opus` as its first understudy and OpenCode second (owner, 2026-10-30: Opus covers Codex authors when Codex fails). Skeptic ballots 1–3 resolve to a Codex primary with only OpenCode behind it; no Claude model appears in their primary or chain. Ballots 4–5 and the launch review resolve to `claude/sonnet` with Codex as the only understudy. A Claude refusal is not handed over (`on_refusal: "halt"`): the call returns null, so a refused ballot is a null ballot (it counts against the gate like a rejection) and a refused review fails as a missing review. Transport failures hand over to Codex as for any other call. Only `claude/sonnet` is routed (never Fable).
14:- The pipeline writes `S/OPERATOR_TAKEAWAY.md` from validated signatures after all stage records, with the raid only in its header. `m5/operator_takeaway.py` accepts optional `--raid`; its Python `takeaway(records, raid=None)` API preserves the old header when omitted. Raid is not added to stage facts or v1 signature IDs.
16:## A/intake/ (written by the intake agent; checked by the pipeline)
17:- benchmark.json, data.json: non-empty JSON objects.
18:- anchors.json: an array, possibly empty; each item has a unique non-empty string `id`, non-empty `quantity` and `source`, finite numeric `published_value`, and `tolerance`. Its length must equal facts.anchors_count. Zero is a valid published value or tolerance.
23:- baseline.json: non-empty repo, build_commands, run_commands and published_configuration, plus commit or pin. `build_commands` lists every command that builds or installs the baseline, including package-manager installs of released binaries, and is never empty. The intake prompt states both. The intake prompt names every key the completeness check reads exactly as the check reads it, as a JSON key: in baseline.json `repo`, `build_commands`, `run_commands`, `published_configuration`, and `commit` or `pin` (`pin` is any non-empty immutable identifier, such as a release, tag or content hash, when no commit exists); in EXECUTION.json `representative_scale`, `inputs`, `outputs` and `timing_scope`. It states that the check reads only these key names, so an equivalent value under another key does not count. The completeness check itself is unchanged.
